Subject: Increased p95 & decode errors after yesterday's model push

Hi Priya,

We started seeing a sharp rise in p95 latency and a ~3.8% increase in token-decoding errors across our inference traffic starting around 02:00 UTC after the model upgrade Redwood applied yesterday. The error spike correlates with peak traffic for our checkout suggestions endpoint.

- ~3.8% token errors (clients seeing truncated responses / early termination).
- Throughput dropped ~18% under sustained load.

This is customer-facing and blocking our holiday promo. Can you triage? I attached a small sample of logs and a csv of request traces.

On Sun, May 30, 2027 at 08:26 AM Priya Natarajan wrote:
> Team — FYI from Amplify (high severity). They report latency, decoding errors, and throughput drop after yesterday's model/quant rollout.

Quick notes from initial triage (logs attached):
- The customer was switched to model redwood-xlarge-v4-q4_0 (4-bit quant profile) as part of the staged rollout.
- We're seeing increased GPU memory churn and a higher frequency of KV cache evictions during long histories which correlates with decode stalls.
- Decoder timeouts appear when the beam/decoding loop hits cache-miss-induced blocking; these surface as token-level truncation errors in the customer traces.
- Tail latency correlates strongly with sequence length distribution spikes at checkout (longer prompts + context).

Immediate mitigations I recommend:
1) Route Amplify traffic back to redwood-xlarge-v4-fp16 (pre-upgrade) — preserves quality and latency; this is the fastest customer-facing fix.
2) If rollback to fp16 is not acceptable, switch them to q8_A (less aggressive quant) for the same model family — should reduce memory churn.
3) As a medium-term fix, we can adjust KV cache thresholds and increase the per-request max_cache_size for their tenant, but this requires a controlled config push and validation.

I attached a short runbook and the perf profile we collected (performance_profile_20270530.csv). I'll follow up with a canary rollback playbook.

Attachments: performance_profile_20270530.csv

—Rishi
SRE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Action plan (immediate, customer-facing):
- We can perform an emergency rollback for Amplify to the pre-upgrade variant (redwood-xlarge-v4-fp16) within the next 90 minutes. That will revert their traffic and should restore previous latency/error levels.
- If you'd prefer no model change, we can temporarily route Amplify to our Dedicated fallback pool (predictable capacity) while we investigate — expect similar mitigation but requires an account-level toggle and a short maintenance window.
- We'll provide a temporary credit for impacted tokens (proposed: 40% credit for the last 24 hours of impacted traffic) pending scope of impact.

Please confirm which option you prefer. If we get sign-off for rollback, Rishi and I will schedule and execute with a short maintenance note to your team.
